scopeNote: NO_SUPPORTED_BOUNDED_RECIPE preserved and NOT re-investigated. No new Driver, no billing proxy, no model send, no ledger refresh. wave03-b-native cap4 remainder stays UNKNOWN and unspendable; E's pilot grant untouched.

plain_json_release_authority.before: resource-facts read plain JSON, so a caller could assemble machine/timeliness/writer fields by hand and receive releaseBarrierSatisfied=true
plain_json_release_authority.after: the only accepted input is the existing authenticated VerifiedRunnerInspection, validated through the single `verified` WeakMap in recovery-transport.ts; no parallel registry was created

token_concurrent_double_spend.before: a token could be consumed twice concurrently because nothing occupied its state before the reservation was awaited
token_concurrent_double_spend.after: state is claimed SYNCHRONOUSLY before any await; a concurrent second consume loses the race and is refused

post_issuance_transport_substitution.before: a token issued for the owned transport could be spent through any other transport the caller supplied
post_issuance_transport_substitution.after: the transport and hook are bound by object identity at issue time and must be the identical objects at consume time

plain_json_gates.before: a caller-supplied gates object claiming everything satisfied was indistinguishable from measured evidence
plain_json_gates.after: gates are snapshotted and frozen into the token; a missing gate is a refusal; a satisfied model gate still needs real model/provider values

caller_override_granted_billing.before: a caller capability override could mark every billing-relevant row supported and switch on billableAdmitted
caller_override_granted_billing.after: overrides may only downgrade billing-relevant rows; billing also requires a measured model/provider carrying provenance, and billingReasons are separate from usability reasons

B1.label: ordinary resource JSON lost its release authority
B1.reusedProof: verifiedRunnerInspection() from recovery-transport.ts; the sole proof WeakMap
B1.requiredAt: actually validated: a proof observed before the required instant is refused as stale_relative_to_requirement, and an unparseable requiredAt is refused rather than skipped
B1.counterexamples: the seven ordinary-JSON shapes are asserted directly and all are refused
B1.positiveControl: a real authenticated server/client pair through serveRunnerRecovery/connectRunnerRecovery; there is deliberately no test-only way to mint a proof

B2.label: barrier semantics on authenticated input
barrierRules: serving is not a release even when every writer is quiescent
open admission keeps a quiescent writer unresolved
partial coverage cannot vouch for a registered resource
a quiescent writer without evidence cannot be audited
no registered resources never satisfies the barrier
one unresolved resource keeps the whole set unresolved
B2.machineBinding: the authenticated socket identity from the proof, never a caller field
B2.observationVsAuthority: a complete-looking plain observation is still not authority; only the authenticated proof is

B3.label: one-use sender bound to immutable request and fixed transport
B3.oneUse: claimed synchronously before the reservation await; never refunded on refusal, throw or unknown
B3.ownerSpoofing: naming the sender's own owner routes through that grant's real ledger audit, which fails, so a caller cannot ride this role's grant

B4.label: the bounded sender E calls directly
B4.entry: createReviewSender({ transport, hook, grant, audit, costBound, hostPolicy }) -> { send, describe }
B4.currentBehaviour: a real send is refused because no per-turn ceiling and no price surface exist; fake send count stays 0 and nothing is reserved
B4.noDescriptorUnlock: a caller cannot switch the bound on with a claim; the measured bound decides and a caller may only make it stricter
B4.descriptorSafety: describe() returns no callable, so E receives no transport or raw command it could use to send another way

B5.label: diagnostics report but never grant
B5.rule: a caller capability override may only downgrade a billing-relevant row; billing additionally requires a measured model/provider with provenance
B5.separation: billingReasons are reported separately from usability reasons, so a missing model identity blocks billing without claiming the executor is unusable
B5.publicProjection: no home or store path in the default projection; private facts are opt-in

notTested: real vendor turn start, stop, question delivery, steer and unknown-send reconciliation
the process-wide epoch high-water mark across a real restart (needs durable storage owned by core/storage)
whether a goal token budget is checked before the first inference of a turn
actual billed amount for any real turn
limitations: the sender cannot prove the caller's process identity; grant authority is the ledger audit, not a boolean
host enforcement is macOS Seatbelt; elsewhere the host capability reports absent
a usable executor is not review admission and not release acceptance
diagnostics describe; they never carry release or billing authority

nextConsumerSteps.main: consume describeResourceFacts only with an authenticated proof; a plain JSON resource summary has no release authority; consume describeRuntime for read-only facts
nextConsumerSteps.D: describeRuntime gives exact executable/profile facts with paths redacted by default; no credential or account home is included
nextConsumerSteps.E: use createReviewSender with the owned transport and your persistent reservation hook; there is no CLI fallback, no descriptor unlock and today the send refuses because the bounded recipe is blocked
